statement: nsys profiling of the reference training step (pre-B1) shows the step is dominated by many small tiled GEMMs and a long tail of tiny kernels including ~194k int/fill launches concentrated in the n-gram value-embedding construction path (ngram_hash_ids + per-layer gather/add), not attention (~5% of step time) or cross-entropy (~1.6%); measured GPU utilization (MFU) ~19%, consistent with a launch-overhead-bound, not compute-bound, step.
possible_confounds: nsys sampling overhead itself perturbs kernel counts slightly
profile taken on a single seed/step window, not averaged across the full 300s run

statement: Round-68 finding (paper 011): disabling the n-gram hash memory (table size -> 1) makes val_bpb nearly flat across data volume (5/8/10 shards: range 0.0035), while the full memory carries the entire data-sensitivity (range 0.1179). The memory's own contribution inverts from -0.029 (helps) at 10 shards to +0.086 (harms) at 5 shards, establishing that the memory is a memorization mechanism whose harm is concentrated at low data.
possible_confounds: single-seed per data level in the original round-68 sweep

statement: 4-arm single-seed factorial (baseline/AttnRes-alone/table-WD-alone/combined) shows combined harm (+0.0715) exceeds the additive prediction from the two individual arms' deltas (+0.0491) by +0.0224 -- a super-additive negative interaction, not independent additive harms.
possible_confounds: AttnRes-alone arm is itself throughput-confounded, so part of the interaction may reflect compounded throughput loss rather than a purely representational interaction
